raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

With decoder SWA bounded replay, every DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill chunk runs the replay layers (20-39) on its last 128 rows, but after the prefill only the prompt's last window is read. This PR replays one row for chunks that end far from the prompt's end. A 124K prompt in 16K chunks now skips 7 of its 8 replay tails. The same idea is DeepSeek DeepInfer's `clip_prefix` rule.

The rule isn't gated on CUDA, so it covers ROCm too. @frida-andersson tested it on 4x MI325X ([numbers](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62817#issuecomment-6370899321)) and is co-author. Her #61682 does the ROCm side of this and she'll close it once this lands.

## Claims

- A prefill chunk that ends at least `decoder_replay_trim_threshold + window` (768 + 128) tokens before its prompt's end replays only its last row, which reads only itself. Chunks within that reach keep the 128-row replay.
- The prompt's last window is computed as before. Greedy outputs on 3 prompts of ~98.6K tokens are identical with and without this change.
- No step reads replay-layer KV that a one-row chunk skipped. Every later chunk whose window still reaches back past a one-row chunk starts its replay window after it and takes the replay batch. A new `ModelState.needs_eager_forward` hook runs such a step eager when it would otherwise keep the whole batch.
- Default decoder replay graph sizes add 1, 2, ..., 64, so a one-row replay batch doesn't pad to 128 rows.
- Single-request TTFT on 2xB200 TP2: 124K -2.4%, 64K -1.6%.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 2xB200 TP2, `--max-model-len 131072`, default `max_num_batched_tokens` 16384, no spec decode. Nightly `df3bd094` with this branch's Python overlaid. Both arms ran in one container as two server boots, with the change switched by a measurement-only env var on a local branch (not part of this PR).

| prompt | chunks (tails skipped) | baseline TTFT | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 126,976 tokens | 8 (7) | 1787.2 ± 11.3 ms | 1744.5 ± 9.6 ms | -2.4% |
| 65,536 tokens | 4 (3) | 877.4 ± 5.1 ms | 863.2 ± 6.4 ms | -1.6% |

These runs and the greedy check below are on `3a584e9`, before merging main. Mean ± std of 3 requests each, concurrency 1, random prompts with a fresh seed per row so nothing hits the prefix cache. That is about 5-6 ms per skipped tail.

Greedy check: 3 chat prompts of 98,664 / 98,515 / 98,610 tokens, each about 6K lines of 12 random words ending with "Which word appears most often above? Answer briefly." Temperature 0, `max_tokens` 64, thinking off. Both arms answer island / forest / meadow, with no reasoning text.

Unit tests on H100 at the current head: 43 passed (`tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py`, `test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py`). New cases cover the one-row rule, the window floor of later chunks (a 200 / 100 / 1 / 26 chunk sequence), the eager hook, the MoE finalize before a short replay batch, and the default graph sizes. The floor and hook cases fail on `7b809c3`, the MoE finalize case on `7ae6c0f`.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_start.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py

vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 131072 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95

vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 126976 --random-output-len 1 \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 3 --seed 101
# 64K row: --random-input-len 65536 --seed 202
```

</details>

## Details

- Why `trim_threshold + window`: steps that keep the whole batch (FULL graphs, PIECEWISE graphs below `decoder_replay_trim_threshold`) let every row read `window - 1` rows back through the batch's SWA metadata. With this reach, the finishing chunk only follows a one-row chunk when it is at least `trim_threshold + window` tokens long, so its own step trims and its window starts inside it. Without replay graphs the reach falls back to `max_num_batched_tokens + window`.
- Any other chunk after a one-row chunk (a short chunk cut by the token budget, the encoder budget or `long_prefill_token_threshold`) gets the window floor and the replay batch, and so does each later chunk until its window no longer reaches the skipped rows. `needs_eager_forward` sends its step to eager when it would keep the whole batch. With default scheduling those chunks sit in full-budget steps above the max capture size, which are eager already.
- The model state records per request where its last one-row chunk ended, until no later chunk's window reaches it. A prefix-cache hit, or a chunk that ran in a whole-batch step, doesn't trigger the floor or the hook.
- `_gather_replay_batch_kernel` takes a per-request KV floor from the host instead of deriving `seq_len - window` itself. Under PCP that floor is the global window start.
- In replay batch steps the layer before the replay layers finalizes its MoE. A one-row or follow-up chunk can put the replay batch on a step of 16 tokens or fewer, where the fused all-reduce + mHC boundary would otherwise leave it unfinalized.
- Prompt-logprob and routed-expert requests keep every row, as before. Under PCP (#62384) every trimmed request keeps its whole window, so the one-row rule is off there.

| 126976 | 4404.5 → 4310.7 (−2.1%, std 1058.8 → 3.6) |

+def test_layer_before_replay_finalizes_moe_in_replay_steps():
+    """The replay batch gathers rows of the encoder output, so in its steps the
+    last encoder layer finalizes its MoE, even for batches that would defer it."""
+    from types import SimpleNamespace

+            return (hidden_states,) * 5 + (None,)
+
+        return forward

+    replay = SimpleNamespace(replay_batch=None)

issue_comments.body:
Thanks for reviewing #61682. I tested this PR on gfx942 (4× MI325X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). The AMD model uses the same replay state as CUDA, and the one-row rule is not gated on CUDA, so this covers ROCm as well. Base is current main `2de0531` plus this change. Chunk cap is 16384. The 256k rows use the same DSpark setup as #61682. `niah_single_2` at 32768 scored 1.0 on both arms (8 samples).

Single request, output length 1, 3 prompts

| Prompt | TTFT (ms) |
|---:|---|
| 65536 | 2237.7 → 2174.8 (−2.8%, std 12.8 → 5.1) |
| 126976 | 4404.5 → 4310.7 (−2.1%, std 1058.8 → 3.6) |

256k → 1k, 20 prompts, 1 warmup. Medians

**Concurrency 2, seed 7**

| Metric | Main | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT (ms) | 13150.1 | 12971.0 | −1.4% |
| TPOT (ms) | 8.13 | 7.85 | −3.4% |
| E2E (ms) | 21596.8 | 21064.1 | −2.5% |
| Output (tok/s) | 94.86 | 96.23 | +1.4% |

TTFT std is 4.2 s on both arms, so that 179 ms is inside the spread. The main TTFT is next to the 13109.6 baseline on #61682.

**Concurrency 6, seed 9**

| Metric | Main | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT (ms) | 23450.4 | 18513.5 | −21% |
| TPOT (ms) | 41.38 | 35.84 | −13% |
| E2E (ms) | 77155.8 | 54582.9 | −29% |
| Output (tok/s) | 71.50 | 106.25 | +49% |

All four move the same way. The spreads are large (TTFT std 21 s → 11 s), and those TTFTs include queueing.

How do you want to go forward with #61682 and this PR?

Thx for testing on MI325X!

#61682 came first, so I'd like to keep it as the one to land. How about I open a PR against your `dsv4-onerow-decoder-replay` branch with the fix from #62817 (the far-from-end gate, the floor for the next chunk, and the eager hook; it isn't gated on ROCm, so it covers CUDA too), and you take it from there? Could you keep me as co-author? I'll close #62817 once it's merged into your branch.

Fine with another way if you prefer.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @ischencheng.

Could you keep me as co-author? I'll close #62817 once it's merged into your branch.
> 
> Fine with another way if you prefer.

I'm fine with landing this PR instead. The fix is already here, so it's simpler to keep one PR. Could you add me as co-author? I'll close #61682 once this lands
